relationship: Unsupported equivalence of life images; not retained
rationale: Job 9:25 explicitly compares life with a swift runner. Job 7:6 calls life lighter than chatter and says it perished in empty hope. The latter does not itself establish the same image of speed; the initially retained general-fragility comparison was removed and remains uncredited.

The source requests an unnamed mediator. The supplied later passage speaks of a thousand death-bearing angels, one not wounding, a person turning to the Lord and renewed flesh; it does not identify an interpreting angel as the mediator requested here.

Job speaks of throwing down and shutting people in so no one can open. The actual Isaiah unit gives David’s glory and uncontested rule; it does not contain the opening-and-shutting wording that motivated the proposal.

Eliphaz recalls Job encouraging weak hands and knees through words. The present source asks for strength in Job’s own mouth and says he will not spare his lips; it does not explicitly promise comfort or strengthening for the friends. That proposed meaning remains unestablished.

relationship: Unresolved heavenly witness identity; not retained
rationale: Job names neither the heavenly witness nor the one who knows with him. First John explicitly identifies Jesus Christ as Advocate with the Father and propitiation for sins. Those identifying and atoning claims cannot be transferred to Job’s unspecified witness from these units alone.

Isaiah explicitly condemns those who call evil good and turn darkness into light. Job speaks of night made day and light near darkness without explicitly assigning that moral reversal to the people described. Shared light vocabulary does not settle that interpretation.
